title: Marc Lawrence Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Is It Worth It?
description: Marc Lawrence Playbook review, checked 7 Nov 2026: real prices, how pay after you win works, what the report card leaves out, and what bettors say.
dek: A long running football newsletter and pick business. Single picks cost $40 to $50 on a pay after you win basis, newsletters run $11 an issue to $155 a season, and pick packages go up to $399 for 30 days. The only record is a report card the seller grades itself, showing win or loss by package name with no line, odds or units.

status.label: Not verified
status.note: Watchdog has not graded a full, time stamped record for Marc Lawrence or any Playbook handicapper. This page reports what we could check and labels everything else.

short_answer: Playbook Sports is a real, long running business. It names an operating company, posts a phone line with hours, publishes prices for every product, and sells a printed football magazine and weekly newsletters that some bettors on forums say they have bought for years. In that sense it is legitimate.

Whether Marc Lawrence's picks make money is a separate question, and nothing we could open answers it. His own report card showed 46 wins, 27 losses and 1 push over 90 days on 7 Nov 2026, but it lists only package names such as "14-0 ATS NFL Perfect System Club Play!" with a W or L. It shows no team, line, odds, star rating or profit, and the headline records on his sales pages did not match the totals we counted from it.

The pay after you win option is the most buyer friendly part: on single guaranteed picks your card is charged only if the purchase shows a net profit. It does not apply to weekly or monthly subscriptions, and it never covers what you lose on the bets. If you buy, start with single picks or one newsletter issue, record every pick with the line you actually got, and judge it after a few hundred plays.

guarantee: Playbook sells its single guaranteed picks two ways. With Pay After You Win, the Picks Policy says your card is authorized but "isn't charged until the game finishes and you show a net profit." Profit is counted at $100 per star, and the package price counts against you: the page's own example says a $35 package with one 5 star winner and two 3 star losers nets minus $195, so you owe nothing. If you pay with Playbook's own Playbucks tokens instead, a losing purchase is returned as replacement tokens, not cash.

The second way, Discount Pre-Paid, costs 20% less up front (a $40 play was $28). The policy states there is "no refund on pre-paid purchases"; a losing purchase comes back only as "Reusable Makeup" tokens for future Playbook picks. The policy also says the guarantee "does NOT apply" to prepaid weekly or monthly subscriptions, so the $149 and $399 packages carry no guarantee. We found no loss terms on the $99 weekend and $349 November packages.

One wording problem: the Today's Picks page calls it "a full money-back promise" and then says a losing pick gets "a free pick in return." Those are not the same thing. Read the Picks Policy, which is the detailed version. No option covers the money you lose on the bets themselves.

claims_note: Pick names do much of the selling. Plays are titled "22-0 ATS College Football Upset Shocker!", "Never Lost CFB Top Kill Play!" or "100% ATS NFL Perfect System Club Play!". Those numbers describe a historical betting angle that fits the game, not the record of Marc's picks. The Black Book systems page lists angles such as 17-0 ATS "since 1980". An angle found by searching decades of past games for a perfect subset says little about the next game, and the report card shows several "100%" and "Never Lost" plays that lost.
The experience figures shift by page: 1975 on the profile, Est. 1984 on the homepage, "Over 40 years" in the banner. None of that is proof of results either way.
record: What is independently verifiable: nothing we could find. We found no full, time stamped log of Marc's picks kept by a third party, no contest standings published by an organizer that we could open, and no court or regulator record involving Marc Lawrence or Playbook in our searches. A forum member said Marc placed 7th in the Westgate SuperContest a few years ago, but we could not find the standings to confirm it.

What is the seller's own marketing: Playbook grades its own experts on an Experts Report Card. On 7 Nov 2026 Marc's page there read 2 wins and 3 losses over 10 days, 14 wins and 9 losses (60.87%) over 30 days, and 46 wins, 27 losses and 1 push (63.01%) over 90 days, back to 9 Aug 2026. Each entry shows only the date, the package title and W, L or T. There is no team, side, line, odds, star rating or units won, so a buyer cannot tell whether those wins made money at the prices they could get. The report card's 90 day button links to the 30 day page; the 90 day list opens only at its own address.

We could not reconcile the sales page headlines with that report card. Counting its entries dated 10 Sep through 26 Oct gives 29 wins, 12 losses and 1 push, not 29-9. Adding 31 Oct and 1 Nov gives 31 wins, 15 losses and 1 push, not 31-12. Playbook may count differently, for example by excluding some plays, but none of the pages we read says how.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Marc Lawrence or Playbook Sports pick is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Marc Lawrence or the Playbook experts perform.
our_data.context: For scale: Playbook's own report card put Marc at 63% over 90 days. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Playbook Sports is thin and mostly forum talk. We found no review site sample we could count. The forum comments split between readers who value the magazine and data and bettors who doubt the pick records.

customers.text: On TheRX newsletters thread, a long time member wrote that Marc claimed 9-1 on 4 and 5 star NFL picks over five weeks, and posted his own tally of 4-3 on 5 star and 5-2 on 4 star NFL picks for that season. Other members replied that he was mixing up the newsletter picks with the paid phone service picks, and one said Marc had not lied. We did not verify either tally.
In a TheRX thread about football services, a member dismissed Marc's picks and claimed he does not bet his own games. No evidence was posted.

In reply, another member called Marc's magazine and newsletter "essential reading" for study, said he had placed 7th in the Westgate SuperContest a few years earlier, and added that nobody hits more than about 57% long term. He praised the research, not the paid picks. We could not confirm the contest finish.

In an older Sportsbook Review thread, a member who subscribed to the newsletter for two seasons said he still buys the Playbook magazine for its technical data, and another called the newsletters useful tools but said following week old picks blindly will not profit. Others said similar information is free online or that midweek newsletters are old news by the time they arrive.

We found no Reddit thread with a real discussion of Playbook Sports, no Better Business Bureau profile we could confirm belongs to playbooksports.com, and no app store listing. Trustpilot blocked our check. We saw no customer testimonials on the Playbook pages we read.

conflicts: Playbook's roster sells picks from other services under its own roof, including Doc's Sports and Jim Feist, and the free pick of the day on 7 Nov 2026 was a Doc's Sports play ending with a pitch for Doc's packages. A buyer should know that Playbook earns from selling other handicappers' picks, not just Marc's.

The daily Coffee Club e-letter on 7 Nov 2026 quoted election odds from "three of the leading offshore sportsbooks," naming Bovada and BetOnline. We did not see sportsbook signup links, promo codes or revenue share links on the Playbook pages we read. Offshore sportsbooks are not licensed by U.S. state regulators.
In September 2024 the football depth chart site Ourlads announced a partnership to feature Playbook and its pay after you win picks. That page is promotional and is not an independent review.
strengths: A named operating company, a phone line with posted hours and a full price list for every product.
Pay after you win on single guaranteed picks: you are billed only if the purchase shows a net profit, with a worked example on the policy page.
Low cost ways to sample: single newsletter issues from $11, a $20 PDF preview guide, a free daily e-letter and a weekly podcast.
A daily report card that does show recent losses, including cold stretches, rather than only hot runs.
concerns: The report card shows W or L by package name only. No line, odds, star rating or units, so profit cannot be checked.
Headline records (29-9, 31-12) did not match our count from the seller's own report card.
No guarantee on the $149 and $399 subscription packages, no stated loss terms on the $99 and $349 specials, and prepaid losses come back as tokens, not cash.
Play names built on "100%" and "Never Lost" historical angles can read like a pick record when they are not one.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: Playbook Sports is a real business run by Playbook Enterprises Inc., with a phone line, published prices and decades of football publications. We could not verify that Marc's picks win over time, because his only record is a report card the seller grades itself, without lines or odds.
How much does Marc Lawrence cost?

On 7 Nov 2026 Marc's single guaranteed picks were $40 or $50 pay after you win ($28 prepaid for a $40 play), his pick packages were $99 for a football weekend, $149 for 7 days, $349 for the November special and $399 for 30 days, and Playbook newsletters ran from $11 an issue to $155 a season.
Does Marc Lawrence have a verified record?

No. Playbook's own report card showed 46 wins, 27 losses and 1 push over 90 days on 7 Nov 2026, but it lists only package names and results, with no line, odds or units, and we found no third party log or contest standings to check it against.

For the money you get Marc's football picks built on historical betting angles, or weekly newsletters and a yearly magazine that some forum bettors value as research. What is unproven is whether his picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays at the lines a buyer can get; pay after you win limits what you pay for losing single picks but not what you lose betting them.
